notes.title: VR Launch Update!
notes.content: [p]Hey Commanders,[/p][p][/p][p]We hope you've been enjoying update 4 of Grit & Valor - 1949! [/p][p][/p][p]We have some news regarding the Steam VR version of our game. We are working hard on updates to address feedback we have recently received. With our focus on improving the experience of Grit & Valor - 1949 for all platforms. The Steam VR version will no longer be launching this week as planned. We apologise for this inconvenience and want to ensure you have the best possible experience when playing.[/p][p][/p][p]Please continue to share any feedback and we promise to keep you updated on any upcoming patches and the launch of the VR version.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you again for your patience and continued support. [/p]

notes.title: Update 4 OUT NOW and VR Launch Update!
notes.content:
[p]Greetings, Commanders![/p][p][/p][p]The fourth post-launch update which comes with a huge list of improvements, balancing and fixes is out now. These include a special focus on post-game content: "[b]Threat Levels[/b]" and a re-work of the [b]Overclock[/b] system.[/p][p][/p][p]We have an update regarding the VR version coming to Steam. Due to an unexpected technical issue with the game, the launch of the VR version has been delayed to next week. We apologise for this inconvenience and want to ensure that you have the best possible experience when playing. We promise to keep you updated on the situation and to let you know once the VR version is officially out next week.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you so much for understanding and for always supporting our game, in the mean time, we hope you enjoy the changes in update 4. We'd love to hear what you think, so let us know by joining our [url="https://discord.gg/xd3dnxUDR5"]Discord server[/url] and sharing your feedback.[/p][p][/p][h2]Threat Level Rising[/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/889b4d26d98cfacd32a00ef871647a05b4606a96.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Threat Levels[/b] have been activated across all regions, marking the beginning of [b]a new post-game campaign[/b]. Each region now comes with [b]five escalating Threat Levels[/b]. The further you push, the tougher enemies become.[/p][p]
Every Threat Level comes with a set of [b]Directives[/b], high-risk challenges that must be completed in a single mission. Succeeding earns you [b]Medals, Command’s new currency[/b] for unlocking higher Threat Levels.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/987381d2077754e3885f131d30e02a68aaa6af07.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Combat balance has been overhauled to match the rising challenge, so expect tougher fights, tighter margins, and deadlier choices. The [b]War Room’s[/b] been retooled to support this new structure. You’ll find Threat Levels front and centre in mission prep, making it easier to track your progress and plan your next deployment.  [/p][p][/p][p]To read more about Threat Levels, check out [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1911860/view/499455821076234421"]our preview post from last week[/url].[/p][p][/p][h2]Overclocks Reforged[/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/d216011ea36869f4876aee63893a74b9e9c897f7.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We also recently posted a preview of the Overclocks re-work! [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1911860/view/499455821076234423"]You can find it here in case you missed it[/url].[/p][p][/p][p][b]Overclocks[/b] are no longer tucked away in the Mech Yard, but now [b]earned in the thick of battle[/b]. You’ll unlock and equip them mid-run, shaping your firepower and tactics in [b]real time[/b]. If you spent Intelligence or Blueprints unlocking Advancements or Overclocks before, Command’s issuing full refunds.[/p][p]
Overclocks are now organised into [b]10 specialist categories[/b], each one pushing your mechs in a new tactical direction. Not every mech can access every category, so you’ll need to know your unit and [b]make your choices count[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/77d295cf6e2695ed4da41bb133d7d5015f3b5687.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Power (the way Overclocks are unlocked) has also changed. It’s now [b]fuelled directly by Boosts and Enhancements[/b]: each one you slot in adds to your [b]Overclock ‘Power’ capacity[/b]. We’ve lowered the thresholds to get you into the action faster, and you’ll see your Power Level front and centre when selecting upgrades. [/p][p][/p][p]We also added a [b]new Overclock reward screen[/b] and upgraded the Squad Overview so you can track your build at a glance.[/p][p]
Command is also dropping [b]43 brand-new Overclocks[/b] into the rotation. Some existing ones have been reworked, others reassigned as Enhancements, and one decommissioned entirely. [/p][p][/p][h1]Changelist[/h1][h2]Threat Levels[/h2][list][*][p]Added Threat Levels which scale the difficulty of the region.[/p][/*][*][p]Added Directives which reward Medals to unlock Threat Levels.[/p][/*][*][p]Added 'View Directives' button to Region Map to track progress.[/p][/*][*][p]End of Run Module rewards quality is now determined by Threat Level instead of Region.[/p][/*][*][p]End of Run rewards now show what Directives were completed on that run.[/p][/*][*][p]Run History now shows what Threat Level it was played on.[/p][list][*][p]Runs from before this update will display as 'Threat Level 1'[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/cb47efa0a919e997a1efa4fcec809e2c7e4f5414.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]Overclocks[/h2][list][*][p]Overclocks have been changed from a meta reward to a run reward.[/p][list][*][p]The Mechanical Surge Advancement and any Overclocks unlocked before this update will have the Intelligence and Blueprints refunded.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Overclocks are now categorised into 10 specialisations with only certain mechs having access to each Overclock specialisation.[/p][/*][*][p]Power for Overclocks is now granted by Boosts and Enhancements, each one equipped giving 1 Power.[/p][/*][*][p]Power required for Overclocks reduced from 4, 12, 20 to 4, 8, 12.[/p][/*][*][p]Mech Power Level is now shown when selecting a Boost or notes.title: Dev Diary: Introducing Threat levels
notes.content:
[p]Greetings, Commanders![/p][p][/p][p]Kevin here, back again with another Developer Diary and today we'll be talking about a brand new feature - [b]Threat Levels[/b][/p][p][/p][p]We’re really excited about this one and it’s probably the biggest change to the game since launch, and will feature in our upcoming Update 4. [/p][p][/p][h3][b]What are Threat levels[/b][/h3][p]Threat Levels allow you to crank up the challenge in every region, letting you take on all 4 Regions with tougher enemies that hit harder, take more damage, and keep you on your toes. [/p][p][/p][p]There are 5 difficulty levels in each Region. Completing 3 Directives at a given level earns you Medals that unlock additional Threat Levels, but not in a strictly linear order - you’ll need to complete Threat Levels in later regions before you can tackle the hardest Threat Levels in Region 1, for instance.[/p][h3] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/eace458b3d2b7583cdfe5c44ff738f8647a7363f.png"][/img]
[b]Why Threat Levels[/b][/h3][p]In a nutshell, Threat Levels give the player more to do in the game but also they:
[/p][list][*][p]Create a smoother, more rewarding sense of progression as you move through regions and tougher difficulties[/p][/*][*][p]Add meaningful end-game content after New Germany[/p][/*][*][p]Encourage replayability and variety by letting you unlock and tackle higher threat levels across regions[/p][/*][*][p]Push players to experiment with squad choices and improve their skills through medals and directives[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/f7824ce2e783a35800feb1b333b3b029ce76f257.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]How Difficult Will it Get?[/b][/h3][p]I asked my colleague Erin who has been regularly testing the new features for a rough breakdown of the difficulty levels:
[/p][list][*][p]Threat Level 1 – git gud this is easy[/p][/*][*][p]Threat Level 2 – okay, not too bad, not too difficult[/p][/*][*][p]Threat Level 3 – uh, struggling a little here[/p][/*][*][p]Threat Level 4 – oh god make it stop[/p][/*][*][p]Threat Level 5 – [b]internal and external screaming![/b][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Anyway, we challenge you all to clear each Threat Level in every Region and look forward to you all telling us how you did![/p][p][/p][p]Thanks for reading our latest Dev Diary and we’re really excited to hearing your feedback on this and all the other new content in Update 4![/p][p][/p][p]Until then, thanks as always for your feedback and support. If you'd like to hear more from us about Grit and Valor, join our Discord server and follow us on social media![/p][p][/p][p][i]- Kevin and The Grit and Valor - 1949 Team[/i][/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary: Overhauling Overclocks!
notes.content:
[p]Greetings, Commanders![/p][p][/p][p]Kevin is back again with another Developer Diary! This time we’re delving into our planned overhaul of the Overclocks system. Thanks to your invaluable feedback, we found ways to make each run feel more unique and satisfying.

Overclocks can be equipped to Mechs in the Mech Yard after earning enough Power (granted by Modules). These give your Mechs a definitive edge during combat, such as by dealing more damage against bosses or reviving your Mech once it reaches 0 HP. However, we felt that this system was going underused for a few reasons:
[/p][list][*][p]Limited variety[/p][/*][*][p]Clear winners for most OP Overclocks (Phoenix Protocol *cough*)[/p][/*][*][p]Hidden away in the Mech Yard[/p][/*][*][p]Grindy to earn Power for Overclock slots[/p][/*][/list][p]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/68661f0552689711604ffa481bacb315312438bd.png"][/img]
In our new system, coming in Update 4 along with VR Mode on 21 August, Overclocks are now accessible through collecting rewards during gameplay. Their other core mechanics remain similar but with some key improvements:
[/p][list][*][p][b]More Overclocks[/b] – a greater variety of Overclocks to choose from[/p][/*][*][p][b]Better run variation[/b] – Overclocks no longer carry over into new runs so different combinations can be chosen each run with no go-to choices[/p][/*][*][p][b]Playstyle defining[/b] - Overclocks are now more playstyle defining. Enhancement and Boosts have been reworked to be more Power focused to complement this[/p][/*][*][p][b]More accessible[/b] – Overclocks are now available during main gameplay and from the get-go [/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]New Overclock Examples[/h3][list][*][p][b]Phalanx Resolve[/b] – When this Mech kills an enemy, a nearby ally restores health[/p][/*][*][p][b]Adrenal Redline[/b] – While at low health, this Mechs fire rate and movement speed are increased every second, stacking up to 100 times[/p][/*][/list][p] 
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/df879bb18ff7d11d09b04188161eea9fb0a3841d.jpg"][/img][/p][p]You'll hear all the full details about the updated Overclocks system in the full Update 4 patch notes on 21 August![/p][p][/p][p]Until then, thanks as always for your feedback and support. If you'd like to hear more from us about Grit and Valor, join our Discord server and follow us on social media![/p][p][/p][p][i]- Kevin and The Grit and Valor - 1949 Team[/i][/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary #4: The Cover Debate Conclusion
notes.content:
[p]Hey everyone, Kevin here again with another Dev Diary!

First off, apologies for the gap in between Dev Diaries, we have been doing a lot of work behind the scenes getting the game ready for the next Major Update and I’m really looking forward to doing a deeper dive into the contents over the coming week.

The focus of this Dev Diary though is the [b]Cover[/b] debate, and our conclusion. Thanks again to everyone who jumped in to give feedback on this, I know cover has been a point of contention for many (including within the dev team) - you’ve all been brilliant about pointing out the good, the bad, and the “huh, that’s weird” moments.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/dac06448a6bdff7336fd20bc7b0e7d5350907d85.png"][/img]
If you missed our earlier post, here’s the short version: [i]Grit and Valor[/i] originally launched with 1-sided cover - walls would only protect you from one direction. Based on your feedback (and a healthy dose of “but… a wall’s a wall, right?”), we decided to trial 2-sided cover. The idea was simple: if there’s a chunk of solid material between you and the enemy, it should block fire from either side. After a good amount of playtesting, here’s where we’ve landed: [/p][h3][b]Our Takeaways[/b][/h3][list][*][p][b]It feels good.[/b] In most situations, 2-sided cover is more intuitive and realistic. You can move a bit more freely, take risks more comfortably, and split forces without feeling overly exposed.[/p][/*][*][p][b]It changes the flow but in a good way.[/b] You can hold ground more dynamically, make more interesting flanking choices, and in some cases avoid the “dash from one safe spot to the next” rhythm, often due to enemies arriving from a different direction and the cover you're next to happens to be facing the wrong way.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Enemies aren’t suddenly superhuman.[/b] We worried they’d start abusing cover against you all the time, but that hasn’t really happened except in some very specific situations (usually tied to poor positioning or unusual map layouts).[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3]The Implication[/h3][p]To get the [i]full[/i] benefit, we needed to rethink level layouts. That meant placing cover so it can be used from multiple angles without clogging movement routes, and balancing cover strength so it lasts long enough to matter without making it a permanent fortress. This ended up being quite a big job as it meant a review and rework of every level in the game. Some needed more tweaks than others but still, a huge undertaking for our small team. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/94089675b463450908d822aa929d9960fea93f3d.gif"][/img][/p][h3]Where we’re at[/h3][p]So, we decided to [b]commit to 2-sided cover[/b] going forward and have now implemented the change. Here’s what you can expect to see in Update 4:  [/p][list][*][p]Stronger, better-positioned cover in key spots.[/p][/*][*][p]Fewer “useless” pieces that block movement without offering good protection.[/p][/*][*][p]More consideration for how both you and the enemy can interact with cover.[/p][/*][/list][p]As always, we’ll be keeping an eye on how this plays once it’s rolled out. So if you find weird edge cases, keep letting us know - your feedback is what helps us improve the game.[/p][p]That’s it for 2-sided cover but watch out for the next Dev Diary showcasing some of the other major changes we’re making for Update 4. [/p][p]Thanks everyone, and see you on the battlefield![/p]

notes.title: Making Grit and Valor Accessible
notes.content: [p]Greetings, Commanders! [/p][p] [/p][p]Accessibility is central to our design philosophy. We believe games are better when [i]everyone[/i] can play. [/p][p]In this post, we’d like to walk you through the accessibility features we’ve implemented in [i][b]Grit and Valor – 1949 [/b][/i]and share a bit about how we approached them. Prefer to sit back and watch? We cover this content in the video below: [/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="KCDaE0Fj4Lk;full"][/previewyoutube][p] [/p][h2][b]🎨 Visual Accessibility[/b] [/h2][p][/p][h3][b]Colourblind Settings[/b] [/h3][p]Unit allegiance and item rarity are partly distinguished by colour, which can be a barrier for colourblind players. To address this, we’ve introduced: [/p][p][/p][list][*][p][b]Dedicated Colourblind Modes[/b] for protanopia, deuteranopia, and tritanopia. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Text Labels for Rarity[/b], so you’ll always see “Common,” “Rare,” etc., alongside the colour. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Custom Colour Selection[/b], allowing players to choose hues that suit their specific vision. [/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]We understand that disabilities including colour blindness exist on a spectrum. It’s not just a matter of being fully colourblind or not. That’s why we designed a colour picker rather than locking players into presets. While we provide standard profiles, we also give players the freedom to choose what works best for [i]their[/i] eyes. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/99aeea590b8d86d5b08381ece5f52a893fa78dfe.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]High Contrast Mode[/b] [/h3][p]Inspired by standout implementations in games like [i]The Last of Us Part II[/i], this mode helps players with low vision by: [/p][list][*][p]Clearly tinting allies, enemies, and objectives (distinct from the behind-wall effect to preserve clarity). [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Removing highlights from dead units, so players can focus on live threats. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Letting players darken or desaturate the environment and skybox via sliders. [/p][/*][/list][p]Much like the colour picker, the contrast sliders came from the understanding that people experience visual limitations to different degrees. Even if you don’t have a disability, features like High Contrast Mode can still help. Some of our own team members with no vision issues prefer to play with it enabled. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/3d44b6e7de3edb5505c5793960ef7e73825dcb08.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]General Visual Features[/b] [/h3][list][*][p]Permanent unit outlines [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Adjustable unit marker sizes [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Off-screen indicators with screen-edge arrows [/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][h2][b]🔊 Audio & UI Accessibility[/b] [/h2][p][/p][h3][b]HUD Feedback for Audio Cues[/b] [/h3][p]For players who can’t rely on sound, we reinforced critical events visually through the unit HUD: [/p][list][*][p]Selected units are clearly mirrored in the HUD [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Damaged units pulse or change in the HUD [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Fallen units display in greyscale [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Incoming hazards are visually signaled on the battlefield [/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3][b]General Audio Features[/b] [/h3][list][*][p]Subtitles in all cutscenes [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Spatial audio support (5.1 & 7.1 surround) to help localize sounds [/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][h2][b]🎮 Input & Sensory Accessibility[/b] [/h2][p][/p][h3][b]Customisable Controls[/b] [/h3][p]Flexible design and controls allow players to customise the gameplay experience to suit their needs and preferences. All controls (keyboard, mouse, and gamepad) are fully re-bindable. This is critical not just for accessibility but for player comfort. [/p][p] [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/68dd9a741c67018de781a21c5b40d7700b0b3480.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Other Features Include:[/b] [/h3][list][*][p]Invertible camera controls [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Haptic feedback at key gameplay moments [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Command Vehicle rumble alerts to warn of imminent destruction [/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][h2][b]💭 Looking Ahead[/b] [/h2][p]With the game fully launched, this is a perfect time for us to reflect and think about future projects. We would like to improve by bringing accessible design into the process [i]earlier, [/i]at the beginning of full production. [/p][p]Something as seemingly small as font size settings means making layout and UI decisions differently from day one. The earlier we include accessibility in the conversation, the more naturally it can be baked into every layer of design. [/p][p] [/p][p]We hope this gives you a clear look at how we’re thinking about accessibility in [i]Grit and Valor – 1949[/i]. Whether it’s a permanent need or just personal preference, we want our tools to help more players enjoy the game their way. [/p][p] [/p][p]Have feedback or ideas? Let us know on Steam or in our [url="https://discord.gg/xd3dnxUDR5"]official Discord[/url]; we’d love to hear from you.[/p][p] [/p][p][i]– [b]The Grit and Valor Team[/b][/i] [/p]

notes.title: AMA: Responses from Developers
notes.content: [p]Greetings, Commanders![/p][p][/p][p]We received fantastic questions from the community, and our developers were delighted to answer. Check out their responses below![/p][h3][/h3][h3]1. Are there plans for future content updates or dlc? [/h3][p]We're currently working on an update that will introduce additional replayability and new play style-changing rewards within a run. And while expanding the game with more fresh content is something we're really excited about, we don't have firm timelines to share yet. But, it's part of our vision for the future.[/p][p][/p][h3]2. Are there any plans for the game to be released on future platforms? [/h3][p]Yes, we recently announced that [i]Grit and Valor[/i] will be coming to [i]PS5, Xbox X/S, Nintendo Switch[/i] and VR Platforms ([i]Meta Quest[/i] , [i]PSVR2[/i], [i]SteamVR[/i]) on the [b]21st August 2025.[/b] The VR version is a free add-on for Steam/PS5 owners. We hope VR players enjoy playing from this new perspective. [/p][p][/p][h3]3. Are new types of Mechs coming? The ones in game already are awesome! But just wanted to know if there was anything new with another unique play style? [/h3][p]We’re really glad to hear you’re enjoying the current Mechs! Designing each one to feel unique and impactful is something we care deeply about. While we’re definitely excited to explore new Mechs in the future, it's too early to confirm. That said, an upcoming update will include a rework of Overclocks to give them a bigger impact on your play style, so you’ll be able to experiment with even more variety using the current Mech line-up.[/p][p][/p][h3]4. What's been your approach to making Grit and Valor accessible, especially from a visual, auditory and motor standpoint? [/h3][p]That’s a great question! Accessibility is a real design challenge in game development, especially given how much interactivity, audio visual feedback, and motor precision is often involved. From the very beginning, we set out to create a more accessible strategy game. That intent shaped a lot of our core design decisions. For instance, keeping the number of controllable units small to avoid overwhelming micromanagement, limiting battlefield size to reduce camera complexity (a common accessibility hurdle), and simplifying the controls wherever possible. In fact, the entire game can be played using just a mouse, even as new features have been added. [/p][p]Our team is passionate about making sure our game is accessible to as many different types of players as possible, and while it’s always an ongoing process, we made sure to include a range of accessibility options at launch to support different player needs. We know there’s still more we can do, and we’re actively listening to feedback from players who rely on these features to help guide our future updates. [/p][p]We also aimed to make our accessibility features adjustable to let players dial in their preferred experience. People have different levels of disability and we wanted to have settings that could adjust to those levels. This inspired options like the colour picker and the re-bindable controls. We hope they benefit as many players as possible.[/p][p]Keep an eye out for a full video in the next couple weeks explaining the processes we used to make the game as accessible as possible.[/p][p][/p][h3]5. What can we expect for future updates? [/h3][p]Future updates will continue to build on player feedback, with our core focus being on increasing the variety of upgrades you’ll see during a run to keep your battles feeling fresh and engaging. We're also increasing replayability and removing some friction points from gameplay. While waiting for these future updates, you can jump into our  recent third update which brings with it enhanced combat feedback, a balance pass on Ability Augments, and new Mech Skins.[/p][p][/p][h3]6. Has the team considered bringing the game to mobile, allowing players to link their accounts and play while travelling? [/h3][p]A mobile version is something we've definitely thought about and the idea of linked accounts allowing you to carry on the fight on-the-go sounds great. Our current focus has been on supporting and expanding the experience on PC and console. So while mobile isn’t in active development right now, it’s a possibility we’d love to explore in the future.[/p][p][/p][h3]7. Are there plans for time-limited events or late-game content like wars or alliance-based challenges?[/h3][p]Our current focus is on strengthening the core gameplay and polishing existing features, but we are looking into post-game systems to add additional challenge for players who have completed the game. Your ideas like time-limited and special events are absolutely on our radar for future updates.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]Want to stay in the loop?[/b][/p][p]Join us on [url="https://discord.gg/8eqDpa88nf"][u]Discord[/u][/url][u] [/u]to chat with the team and community anytime! Don’t forget to follow [i]Grit and Valor - 1949[/i] on social media for all the latest updates, events, and sneak peeks.[/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary #3: Shifting progression Emphasis
notes.content: [p]Hey everyone – Kevin here again with another Dev Diary! [/p][p][/p][p]First off, a big thank you for all the positive feedback on the latest update, it really means a lot to the team. We’re very happy to see it landing well with so many of you. That said, we know there’s still plenty of work to do, so please keep the feedback coming![/p][p][/p][p]This week, I wanted to talk a bit about [b]progression[/b]. We’ve been hearing from some players that the game can feel a bit grindy, like runs don’t stand much of a chance unless you’ve already sunk a good amount of time into upgrading your squad at the Resistance Base.[/p][p][/p][p]When we set out to make [i]Grit and Valor[/i], our goal was to create that classic roguelite loop: try, fail, learn, improve, repeat. But from your feedback, it sounds like that loop is leaning more toward frustration than fun in some cases.[/p][p][/p][p]Just before I get into what we're thinking, I will mention that Update #1 went some way to addressing the 'grind' concerns already by making sure players start with all 3 mechs in their squad from the start, but clearly there is more to be done.[/p][p][/p][p]So here’s what we’re thinking (still early days, so nothing final yet): we want to [b]ease up on how heavily the game leans on meta progression[/b], as that seems to be driving some of the grind. Instead, we’re planning to [b]boost the strength, impact and variety of run rewards[/b], so each session feels more rewarding and meaningful on its own. [/p][p][/p][p]We’re also looking at moving [b]Overclocks into the run itself[/b], which should help create more exciting (and varied) power spikes during a run, and make things feel less dependent on long-term upgrades. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/e450248335dddeb565b364474780a60f999e2a62.png"][/img][/p][p]We’re not going full roguelike, but we are thinking to nudge things more in that direction.[/p][p]If this feels good in testing, we’ll follow it up with a [b]balance pass[/b], just to make sure the stronger run rewards don’t end up making things too easy if you happen to stumble on a really amazing build, especially since we know some of you are already breezing through the game! This might also come alongside some other difficulty changes if needed.[/p][p][/p][p]Another thing we know is adding to that grindy feeling is the [b]lack of level variety[/b]. We’ve actually started prototyping some new level types, and eagle-eyed players might’ve noticed that a new level type was originally planned to go out with Update 2. These are closely tied to the progression changes we’re working on, so we’ve decided to hold them back until that side of things is in a better place.[/p][p][/p][p]Huge thanks for sticking with us, and for helping shape the game with every new update.[/p][p][/p][p]Thanks everyone, have an awesome weekend![/p]

notes.title: Post-Launch Update 2: Chain of Command

Greetings, Commanders!

With this update, our goal is to put tactical command firmly in your hands. We're introducing new tools to coordinate your squad with greater precision, whether it’s by locking onto high-value targets, setting unit-specific priorities, or issuing instant regroup orders in the heat of battle. 

Every change is designed to deepen your strategic options and reward smart decision-making on the field.

[h2]Tactical Improvements[/h2]

[h3]New Command: Regroup[/h3]

When things get messy, you need to pull back fast and smart. That’s where Regroup comes in. One command, and every unit in your squad will rally to a point you choose. No fumbling, no delay. You can issue it with a quick click of the Regroup button at the bottom right of your HUD, or by using your assigned keyboard or gamepad binding. Use it wisely, it might just save your squad.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/edaafae6c0157e2ee85ca371c01149c4760cc8d4.gif[/img]
[h3]New System: Target Priorities[/h3]

Outnumbered? Surrounded? Doesn’t matter, what matters is who you hit first. With the new Target Priorities system, each of your mechs follow orders the way you see fit. You set the rules, they execute. Choose from the following priorities:
[list]
[*] Type
[*] Weak
[*] Healthy
[*] Injured
[*] Far
[*] Close
[/list] Access this feature through the Squad Overview by clicking the button on your HUD, or use your assigned keyboard or gamepad binding. Once you’re in, you’ll see toggles on each unit to set their priorities.

notes.title: Dev Diary #2: Cover Deep Dive
notes.content:
Hey everyone – Kevin here again with another Dev Diary! This time, we’re diving deeper into one of the core gameplay mechanics: Cover.

Since launch, we’ve gotten a lot of feedback about how cover works in the game – especially around our decision to make it 1-sided (offers protection in only one direction) instead of 2-sided (protection from both directions).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/bc59c5ddbdf7238dd7f7e1f8581decc71f6b3b98.png[/img]

To be honest, most of the feedback has leaned critical, or at least confused. Outside of our dev team, not many players have spoken in favor of 1-sided cover – and even within the team, there are folks who’d prefer the 2-sided approach.

These kinds of design choices are always tricky during development, so I wanted to share a bit of insight into how we made the call, and what the pros and cons of each setup look like.

[b]1-sided Cover[/b]
Pros:
[list]
[*] Encourages more strategic positioning – players need to be mindful of where enemies are coming from.
[*] Promotes level exploration, as players move around to find cover that works based on the direction of threat.
[*] Gives players a tactical advantage – enemies are much less likely to benefit from cover.
[*] Cons:
[*] Doesn’t always make sense visually – why would a wall only protect from one side?
[*] Can be frustrating when a seemingly good piece of cover becomes useless just because enemies show up from the "wrong" direction.
[/list]
[b]2-sided Cover[/b]
Pros:
[list]
[*] Feels more intuitive and realistic – a wall should offer protection on both sides.
[*] Makes cover more universally useful, which could help reinforce it as a core mechanic instead of something players forget about.
[*] It adds to the tactical challenge – if enemies use cover against you, that’s on your positioning. You either take the cover yourself or deny it to the enemy by repositioning.
[/list]
Cons:
[list]
[*] Players might end up dancing around a single block of cover depending on enemy spawns, rather than moving around the map. (see diagram below).
[*] If cover takes damage from both sides, it could get destroyed really quickly. That might balance things out and make players move around the map more, but could also make cover feel weak or temporary.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/44721ffad3fdabcc72c03dd00423b6e418a0bbcb.png[/img]
We have started to prototype 2-sided cover and discovered a couple of bugs so far but generally the bulk of the work would come from going into each level and making sure:
[olist]
[*] Cover isn’t  too advantageous if it suddenly became 2-sided, and possibly therefore stripping some cover out or moving it around.
[*] Cover isn’t too weak now it takes damage from both sides and needs a further balance pass on each level (or again some rearrangement).
[/olist]
As you can probably tell, we’re still torn on which direction to go. We’d love to hear your thoughts to help us decide!

In the meantime, we’ll keep testing and share more updates in the next Dev Diary.

Thanks for reading everyone – and enjoy your weekend!
Kevin

notes.title: Dev Diary #1: Post-Launch Reflections
notes.content:
Hi everyone, Kevin here — Producer on the project.

It’s now been around six weeks since the game launched, and we’ve had some time to reflect on the release, the state of the game, and all the feedback we've received. I wanted to take a moment to share some of those reflections with you and give a clearer picture of where we’re heading.

[h3]Launch and First Impressions[/h3]
Game launches are never easy. You spend years building something, then release it into the world and hope that players connect with it as deeply as you do. It’s an emotional moment — a mix of relief, joy, and (let’s be honest) a bit of fear, and a lot of hitting "refresh" on Steam reviews!
That said, we’re really proud of the game we released. The launch went smoothly overall, and while reviews have ranged from okay to good, we’re taking everything on board. A 77% review score in the strategy genre isn’t bad — especially given how savvy and discerning this audience is. The general consensus seems to be: “There’s a solid foundation here, but room for improvement.” We agree.

[h3]Top Themes in Player Feedback[/h3]
Here's a quick summary of the key feedback we've seen so far:

[list]
[*] Core gameplay is fun but lacks tactical depth
[*] Core gameplay is fun but lacks variety (e.g., things you experience in runs and ability to change things up mid-run)
[*] The roguelite grind can feel frustrating
[*] Game balance needs further refinement
[*] Certain gameplay elements feel frustrating (notably: Hazards, repetitive VO, and the Cover system)
[*] Some players expected a turn-based experience similar to Into the Breach
[/list]

There’s a lot to unpack here. We're a small team, so we’re taking things step by step — prioritising, testing, and listening. While I can’t promise every piece of feedback will be addressed immediately, I can promise to keep sharing what we’re working on and to keep the conversation going.

[h3]What We're Working on Right Now[/h3]
Here’s what we’re currently focused on (and I’ll dive into these more in future posts — some of them deserve their own breakdown):

[h3]Cover - 1-sided vs. 2-sided[/h3]
There’s been plenty of feedback to say that cover should be two-sided, one-sided cover doesn’t make sense etc. and we understand where people are coming from. Cover has always been one-sided to make it a clear tactical advantage to the player rather than something that enemies will also benefit from....but given the weight of feedback, two-sided cover is something we’re testing out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/e98027c64010b48f74600dc23b7282d4cee4556d.gif[/img]

[h3]Re-group Command & Enemy Prioritisation[/h3]
Players have been asking for more tactical control and less micro-management — a tricky balance, but one we’re working toward. To help with that, we’ve been testing a new regroup command, along with a feature that lets you set priority levels for your units. Both of these should cut down on the need for constant individual clicks and repositioning, while still giving you room to plan more strategically — without slowing things down for players who prefer a more fast-paced, action-heavy style.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/95ad85828193e497b3f56d2496905d714d037232.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/5764ba85225e64d643b60edb8e1152a7832caa61.gif[/img]

[h3]Surfacing more useful information[/h3]
Players have been asking for clearer, more detailed info to help make better choices around upgrades and progression. We’re updating menus and tooltips to show more stats — including comparisons where it makes sense. So far, we’ve focused on areas like the Pilot Barracks and Ability stats, Mechyard tooltips, and the run overview. We’ll keep refining and expanding as we go.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/602dff698a5d29165312506991ae65fc71ed6931.png[/img]

That’s it for now — just a quick update to let you know where our heads are at. Massive thanks to everyone who’s played the game, shared feedback, or just taken the time to care. It really does mean a lot.

Thanks everyone,
Kevin

notes.title: Patch Notes: Display Settings and Other Fixes
notes.content:
Greeting, Commanders!

Following your bug reports and feedback we have implemented the following changes:

[h3]Display Settings Fixes[/h3]
We have overhauled the system for managing display settings to address cases that were not fixed by the previous patch. The changes include:
[list]
[*] When you change the resolution, display or window mode and select Apply in the Settings menu, the game now saves your changes without re-applying them.
[*] When you make changes in the Settings menu and select Revert, the game applies your previously saved display settings and refreshes the settings text once the changes have finished applying.
[*] When you select Defaults from the Settings menu, the game returns to your main display (the first one in the Display list) and uses that display's native resolution in Borderless window mode. If the native resolution is reported as portrait, the game translates it to landscape.
[/list]
[h3]Known Issues and Limitations[/h3]
[list]
[*] The UI is designed for a minimum aspect ratio of 16:10 (commonly used on laptops and handhelds), so we don't recommend using any narrower resolutions. The 4:3 and 5:4 resolutions are automatically filtered out.
[*] Portrait displays such as vertical monitors are not supported, so the game may behave unexpectedly if you try to move the game window to them.
[*] When setting the Window Mode to Fullscreen and using a resolution other than the display's native resolution, the game may not display correctly. If you need to use a non-native resolution, we recommend using Borderless window mode.
[*] You may see unusual resolutions in the list which are larger than your display's native resolution (e.g. some 1440p monitors may also list 4K as an option). This is normal as the game reads from the same list of resolutions available in Windows Display Settings, even if they cannot be applied.
[/list]
[b]Please Note[/b]
If the game launches in an incorrect resolution or does not let you select a playable resolution after installing this patch, please follow these troubleshooting guidelines:

[b]Reset Settings to Defaults[/b]
The game may be trying to load an invalid resolution that was saved in a previous patch, so please try reverting your settings to defaults. If you cannot do this in-game, follow these steps:
[olist]
[*] Close the game.
[*] Delete your Settings.ini file which can be found in this folder: %USERNAME%/AppData/LocalLow/MilkyTea/Grit and Valor
[*] Launch the game again.
[/olist]
[b]Report a Bug[/b]
If you have tried the above and the game still does not display correctly, please follow these steps to send us more information so we can debug the issue:
[olist]
[*] In your Steam Library, right-click the game and select Properties, then go to the Betas tab and enter the password fixthescreens. 
[*] Opt into the mt_debug_display branch which should appear.
[*] Download and install the beta update.
[*] Launch the game.
[*] Open the Display Debugger menu from the top of the screen. This menu is centered horizontally so it should be accessible even if the game launches in a narrow resolution.
[*] Take a screenshot of the game while the Display Debugger menu is open (press F12 to capture via Steam).
[*] Upload your screenshot and send it to us either in this Steam discussion or in the bug-reports channel on the Grit and Valor Discord.
[/olist]
[h3]Other Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed Bomber Plane not appearing in the Advanced Combat levels in New Germany.
[*] Fixed dead units causing navigation issues and units to spin on the spot.
[*] Fixed tile issues in Western Europe levels in which inaccessible tiles were selectable, causing mech pathing issues.
[/list]
Thanks for your patience while we have dealt with these bug reports. We appreciate all the feedback and will continue investigating any future reports. You can share your experiences here on Steam or via the official [url=https://discord.gg/8eqDpa88nf]Discord[/url].

[i]The Grit and Valor - 1949 Team[/i]

notes.title: Mech Analysis: Leadslug
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders! 

Today we’re examining the Leadslug, a Ballistic-Class Mech manufactured by Sebika Ballistics. Its devastating shotguns unleash a ferocious spread of piercing rounds, causing destruction to anything in its path. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/a8b7eb1f5aec721c51564858dfe8d44f1cd6e975.jpg[/img]

[h3]BASE STATS [/h3]
[list]
[*] Health: 500 
[*] Armor: 0  
[*] Repair: 0  
[*] Movement Speed: 15 
[*] Damage: 15 
[*] Weapon Range: 2 
[*] Fire Rate: 120 
[*] Weakness Damage: 50% 
[*] High Ground Damage: 20%  
[*] Critical Chance: 0%  
[*] Critical Damage: 100% 
[/list]
The Leadslug has consistent stats across the board with respectable movement speed, health, and standard critical/weakness damage output. Its key drawback is it’s below-average weapon-range of two tiles, meaning this mech needs to get up close and personal to confront enemies.  

It makes up for this with a high fire rate, ensuring that once you engage, you’ll be spraying Axis units with hail of bullets from its dual shotguns and extinguishing them quickly. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/1f1cb24d787f554a35b155e16b95e1174336a740.jpg[/img]

[h3]ABILITY PAIRINGS [/h3]
As a solid all-round unit, the Leadslug has flexible options for ability pairings. However we do have some preferences within the three provided by your starting pilots: 

[list]
[*] [b]Archie Miller - Mech Jet:[/b] this is a prime choice since the Leadslug only has a weapon range of two tiles. Being able to jump in to engage your enemies quickly helps overcome any vulnerability from being exposed to Axis units with longer range for too long. 

[*] [b]Emilia Rochefort - Mechano-Arm:[/b] another way to circumvent the Leadslug’s requirement to get close to enemies is with the Mechano-Arm to help it tank incoming damage. This is a great choice which enables the mech to play a bruiser-style role on the squad and relieve pressure from your other units. 

[*] [b]Jan Novak - Deploy Mines:[/b] these are our third choice from the starting lineup. With a respectable movement speed, the Leadslug can get around the map well enough to drop mines in prime locations. However, these do less than the other two abilities to make up for the mech’s key weakness. 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/0b002ed627d6f8df2cd02780405241f071e107e8.jpg[/img]

Overall, the Leadslug is an impressive staple of the squad and is sure to output plenty of damage. If you can keep it repaired or armoured-up throughout a run, it’s sure to pay you back by obliterating your foes. Stay tuned for more intel on the remaining mech models! 

Stay up to date on game news and more by joining us on Discord!

notes.title: Mech Analysis: Clusterstorm
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders! 

It’s time to meet Clusterstorm, another Explosive Class mech! This absolute unit fires repeated cluster bombs which raze sections of the battlefield, leaving enemy units nowhere to flee. Use it to thin out entire wave of incoming foes for your other mechs to pick off at their leisure. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/f47073575c4483d7fc09179b78a31cdab46afcdf.jpg[/img]
[h3]KEY STATISTICS[/h3] 
The Clusterstorm boasts a reliable spread of stats. Dealing 20 base damage per rocket raises the ceiling of each volley it fires. Complimented by a weapon range of 3 tiles, makes this perfect for dealing damage across entire squads of enemies. 

With a base health stat of 500, the Clusterstorm can be vulnerable compared to tankier units. Make sure to either get in first with enough firepower to wipe out anything that attacks it quickly or use other mechs to bear the brunt of the damage. 

A high base movement speed of 20 leaves the Clusterstorm surprisingly agile with the ability to reposition and make up for it’s lower health rating. If you ever need split the squad, it can quickly move across the map to support your remaining units where needed. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/e5b043241f795ccd7543d91b5ae3f8d5fe02e22f.jpg[/img]
[h3]ABILITY PAIRINGS[/h3] 
Paired with the right ability, the Clusterstorm can be made even more effective in combat. Here some considerations for using it with the three abilities provided by your starting pilots: 

[b]Archie Miller - Mech Jet:[/b] Double down on the Clusterstorm’s high rate of movement by allowing it to travel even faster with this jump ability. Doing so means you can cover ground faster than any other unit, to defend or capture objectives, gather air-dropped enhancements, and quickly return to the fight. 

[b]Jan Novak - Deploy Mines:[/b] Being able to move quickly by default also makes the mines an interesting option. Allow your slower mechs to hold down the fort while sending out the Clusterstorm to strategic positions to place mines. 

[b]Emilia Rochefort - Mechano-arm:[/b] To make up for the Clusterstorms key weakness (low health), you can give it this self-healing ability to make a more well-rounded unit. Allowing this mech to sustain additional damage will give it enough time to deal damage and defeat most enemies. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/5111f57cabea4e3ff2307d7bb29d476c22ca7d39.jpg[/img]
The Clusterstorm is an asset to any squad with its wide range of applications and ability to pair well with any given pilot. It comes with some additional pressure to protect another unit beyond just the Command Vehicle, but if you take of it, the Clusterstorm will take care of you back with efficiency in clearing out enemies. We have two more mech analyses to go to complete the set, so stay tuned for further intel! 

Stay up to date on game news and more by joining us on Discord! 

[i]The Grit and Valor – 1949 Team[/i]

notes.title: Mech Analysis: Warbringer
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders! 

Introducing the Warbringer, an Explosive Class mech designed for maximum impact. Manufactured by Warhead, this heavy-duty powerhouse comes equipped with dual launchers, allowing it to strike multiple enemies simultaneously. Whether bombarding enemy squads or softening up fortified positions, the Warbringer ensures no target is safe from its devastating firepower. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/0c2e7000bbe81fc8579477bc3b0259321ea2a5ed.jpg[/img]
[h3]KEY STATISTICS [/h3]
The Warbringer is a force to be reckoned with in any battle, thanks to its high Fire Rate and ability to deal sustained damage across multiple targets. While its Damage per shot is modest, its rapid Fire Rate ensures it can consistently lay down heavy fire over a wide area, overwhelming your enemies and supporting the squad. 

The Warbringer can take considerable damage before going down, though it relies on your positioning and support to endure. Movement Speed is moderate, making it less nimble than faster mechs but still capable of staying in combat without being too slow. 

Its Weapon Range allows it to engage most threats at medium distances while remaining out of range from many close-combat enemies. Its rapid fire rate ensures plenty of opportunities for consistent damage output. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/3caa84b98593b2a6f51d3102cf340bd8b034f344.png[/img]
[h3]ABILITY PAIRINGS [/h3]
With the right ability pairings, the warbringer can turn it into a relentless force on the battlefield. 

[b]Archie Miller - Mech Jet:[/b] The Warbringer's moderate speed means it can struggle to reposition quickly. The Mech Jet ability allows it to traverse the battlefield with ease, getting into better firing positions or escaping overwhelming encounters. This can be especially useful when taking advantage of the High Ground Damage bonus, letting it reach elevated terrain for maximum impact. 

[b]Jan Novak - Deploy Mines:[/b] Since the Warbringer's rapid firepower can lock down areas, Deploy Mines provides an excellent defensive tool to complement its offensive capabilities. Place mines ensuresenemies take additional damage while trying to evade its barrage. 

[b]Emilia Rochefort - Mechano-arm:[/b] The Mechano-arm provides much-needed health regeneration, allowing it to remain in combat longer and sustain its relentless firepower without requiring frequent retreats. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/5a1a3f7e5d8993d8ec49d71cc2dc160f07c2e09a.png[/img]

With the right strategy, the Warbringer becomes an unstoppable force, raining down destruction on multiple enemies at once. Its high fire rate and area control make it a formidable asset in any squad, especially when paired with abilities that enhance its positioning, survivability, and battlefield dominance. Stay tuned for more intel on the remaining mech models!

notes.title: Mech Analysis: Vulcano
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders! 

Today’s briefing covers the Vulcano, a fire class mech manufactured by Forge Industries. It's volcanic cannon rains molten destruction in an area on and around its enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/734dcf48cb31cf173ad9e97116d0872ec1abf8d2.jpg[/img]

[h3]KEY STATISTICS[/h3] 
The Vulcano brings overwhelming firepower to the battlefield as a Fire Class mech, specializing in close-to-mid-range engagements. Its high base Damage and steady Fire Rate allow it to unleash relentless attacks, making it a force to be reckoned with in prolonged skirmishes. 

With a solid Health pool but low Movement Speed, the Vulcano is best if you position it on the front lines where it can sustain engagements while dealing heavy damage. Its moderate Weapon Range gives it flexibility, allowing it to handle multiple enemy types without being forced into direct melee combat. 

Commanders should capitalize on Weakness Damage and High Ground advantages, ensuring that the Vulcano’s attacks land with maximum impact. When properly supported and positioned, this mech can turn the tide of battle with sheer destructive force. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/449824d6749f114d1fbeabb115b5817b1407e44e.gif[/img]

[h3]ABILITY PAIRINGS[/h3] 
The Vulcano excels when paired with the resistance pilots to make up for its low mobility, enhance its area control, or sustain its frontline presence. 

[b]Archie Miller – Mech Jet:[/b] The Vulcano’s low Movement Speed can make it vulnerable to being outmaneuvered. Mech Jet provides much-needed mobility, allowing it to reposition quickly, close gaps, or escape dangerous situations. 

[b]Jan Novak – Deploy Mines:[/b] The Vulcano’s high base Damage and moderate range make it ideal for area control, and Deploy Mines reinforces this strength. Placing mines in strategic areas or near objectives ensures that enemies take significant damage before even engaging, complementing the Vulcano’s aggressive playstyle. 

[b]Emilia Rochefort – Mechano-arm:[/b] Mechano-arm keeps the Vulcano in the fight longer, reducing downtime and allowing it to continuously unleash its devastating firepower without needing frequent retreats. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/775bfd92283eeb178950d87f64f6337430541dd8.gif[/img]

With the right strategy, the Vulcano becomes an unstoppable force, delivering relentless firepower while holding the line against enemy advances. When properly supported, it can dominate the battlefield with sheer destructive capability. Stay tuned for further reports on the remaining mech models.

notes.title: Mech Analysis: The Steelhawk & Steam Next Fest!
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders! 

We are delighted to be part of Steam Next Fest this year starting from now! If you haven't already, we would love it if you played our demo and shared your feedback here on Steam and in [url=https://discord.com/invite/Us8nCSbP8A]Discord[/url].

Today’s briefing covers the Steelhawk, a precision-focused Ballistic Class mech designed for long-range eliminations. Manufactured by Sebika Ballistics, this mech wields a colossal sniper rifle capable of striking your targets from extreme distances. With an increased chance to deal critical hits, the Steelhawk is the perfect choice for those who favour high-impact, calculated shots over sustained fire.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/5fa68fa877914387b1aef0f9db861cab8fe55557.jpg[/img]
[h3]KEY STATISTICS[/h3] 

The Steelhawk is a precision powerhouse, built for long-range combat and high-damage critical hits. As a Ballistic Class mech, it specializes in single, devastating shots rather than rapid-fire engagements. With a long Weapon Range, it can strike enemies from afar, making it ideal for picking off key targets before they can retaliate. 

Its increased Critical Chance sets it apart, giving it a much higher probability of landing devastating critical hits. However, with moderate Health, the Steelhawk isn’t built for direct engagements. Its low Fire Rate means every shot must count, as it lacks the sustained output of other mechs. Commanders should focus on maintaining distance, using cover, and prioritizing targets to maximize its lethality on the battlefield. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/662e11438c3928e3f0ad55a1b1e5f568104d8239.gif[/img]

[h3]ABILITY PAIRINGS[/h3] 
The Steelhawk excels when paired with abilities that enhance its positioning, survivability, or battlefield control. 

[b]Archie Miller – Mech Jet:[/b] The added mobility of Mech Jet allows the Steelhawk to quickly reposition, reaching vantage points that maximize its High Ground Damage bonus. Whether escaping threats or securing the perfect sniping spot, this ability ensures the Steelhawk remains a dominant force at long range. 

[b]Jan Novak – Deploy Mines:[/b] The Steelhawk benefits greatly from Deploy Mines to secure its surroundings. Place your mines near chokepoints or along flanking routes helps prevent enemies from closing the gap, keeping the Steelhawk free to focus on precision eliminations. 

[b]Emilia Rochefort – Mechano-arm:[/b] The Steelhawk’s moderate health make sustain important for prolonged engagements. Mechano-arm provides vital repairs, allowing the mech to maintain its position and continue dealing devastating critical hits without needing to retreat too often. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/0bc27df039acbb3fa657427bb4cbfa2e37613b73.gif[/img]

This intel should aid in your strategic deployment of the Steelhawk, Commander! When utilized effectively, it becomes an invaluable asset for long-range support, delivering precise and devastating strikes from a safe distance. Keep an eye out for further reports on the remaining mech models.

notes.title: Update: Control Scheme Improvements
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders!

Thank you as ever for your determined efforts to liberate the British Isles! Your feedback and reviews throughout the demo have been incredibly helpful. Based on your suggestions, we’re making changes to the controls. These are now live in the demo and will also feature in the final release on 26 March.

[b]NOTE: Existing players will need to reset controls to default for some of these changes to take effect.[/b]

[h2]General Improvements[/h2]
[h3]Unit Cycling[/h3]
Previously, Cycling Units would default to the same mech, making moving your whole squad tedious with this method. It looked something like:
[olist]
[*] Press Cycle Units which would select the first unit (e.g. Ironclad).
[*] Move Ironclad to a tile, at which point the Ironclad gets deselected.
[*] Press Cycle Units, which selects the Ironclad again.
[*] Press Cycle Units again for it to then Select the next unit (e.g. Draqan).
[/olist]
Now, the system will automatically move along to the next unit in order by default to help you cycle through them more quickly.

[h2]Keyboard + Mouse Changes[/h2]
[h3]Left Click/Right Click[/h3]
Units are now selected with the left mouse button and moves with the right mouse button by default. This is more in line with other RTT and RTS games. The units’ colliders have also increased in size, making them easier to select quickly. We hope this makes manoeuvring your squad more fluid!
Gamepad and touch controls remain in the one-button style for convenience on those control schemes.

[h2]Gamepad Changes[/h2]
[h3]Unit Cycling[/h3]
Cycling through units is now bound to the left/right bumpers by default (previously left/right on the d-pad). This allows you to cycle through units at the same time as controlling the camera more easily.

[h3]Freeze Time[/h3]
Moving the unit cycling to bumpers has displaced the default for the freeze-time binding. This is now moved to X (Button West), the last remaining free face button.

Thanks once again for all your suggestions! We firmly believe these changes will greatly improve the experience of quickly manoeuvring your squad. Let us know what you think, here on Steam and in our official Discord.

[b]REMINDER: Existing players will need to reset controls to default for some of these changes to take effect.[/b]

[i]The Grit and Valor – 1949 Team[/i]

notes.title: Mech Analysis: The Thunderhead
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders! 

Today’s briefing contains an analysis of the Thunderhead. This Explosive Class mech is the embodiment of heavy artillery dominance. Manufactured by Warhead, it comes equipped with a pair of powerful mortar cannons, each launching devastating high-explosive shells at its targets. With its overwhelming firepower, the Thunderhead is perfect for raining destruction from a distance, making it an invaluable asset for squads that favour long-range bombardment. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/7857a72b78a40921de22cda50692fc76d53810b7.jpg[/img]
[h3]KEY STATISTICS [/h3]
The Thunderhead is the powerhouse of [strike]the cell[/strike] long-range destruction. As an Explosive Class mech, it relies on its dual mortar cannons to deliver high-damage blasts.  

However, with a low Fire Rate and slow Movement Speed, the Thunderhead isn’t built for rapid engagements or quick repositioning. Instead, it thrives when you hold key positions, raining down fire from a distance thanks to its extended Weapon Range. Commanders should prioritize positioning, ensuring the Thunderhead remains protected while it shells enemy forces from afar. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/942f1335e41fd49b07755fdb1a1d9a2bdc613208.gif[/img]

[h3]ABILITY PAIRINGS [/h3]
The Thunderhead is a devastating long-range mech, but its slow Movement Speed and low Fire Rate mean it requires careful positioning and support to maximize its effectiveness. These ability pairings will help it stay in the fight and deliver its full explosive potential: 

[list][*] [b]Archie Miller – Mech Jet:[/b] While the Thunderhead is built for long-range engagements, its low mobility makes it vulnerable when caught in close combat. Mech Jet allows you to reposition it quickly, either to gain a better vantage point or escape dangerous situations. This ability is especially useful for securing high ground, where the Thunderhead’s High Ground Damage bonus can deal even more destruction. 
[*] [b]Jan Novak – Deploy Mines:[/b] Given its slow Fire Rate, the Thunderhead can struggle against fast-moving enemies who close the distance before it can fire. Deploy Mines provides an extra layer of defense, creating deadly zones that punish aggressive enemies before they reach firing range. Combined with its explosive mortar blasts, this pairing turns the battlefield into a minefield of destruction. 
[*] [b]Emilia Rochefort – Mechano-arm:[/b] The Thunderhead is at risk of being overrun if enemies manage to push past its bombardment. The Mechano-arm offers health regeneration, allowing it to stay in battle longer and maintain sustained fire from the backlines.  [/list]
These ability pairings allow the Thunderhead to overcome its weaknesses and remain a dominant force in long-range warfare. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/3fa10862c63aa6bdae4f3d609a1b031fd09689a3.gif[/img]

We hope this analysis helps you make the most of the Thunderhead! With the right positioning and support, it can annihilate enemies from a distance, providing your squad with unmatched firepower. Stay tuned for further reports on the remaining mech models.

notes.title: Mech Analysis: The Draqan
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders!

This report brings intel regarding the Draqan, a Fire Class mech. Manufactured by Forge Industries, this fearsome machine is built for destruction. Its flamethrowers engulf all enemy forces caught in their path, leaving nothing but scorched wreckage in its wake. While specializing in fiery devastation, it remains a well-rounded choice for commanders that require aggressive frontline power.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/d04ebbf526ddc65fa233c706138e821c40da7e29.jpg[/img]

The Draqan is a relentless force on the battlefield, bringing the full destructive power of the Fire Class to bear. Equipped with devastating flamethrowers, this mech specializes in close-quarters combat, incinerating anything in its path with a high Fire Rate and consistent Damage output. 

With its high Mobility, you can swiftly reposition the Draqan to control key areas, secure Enhancements drops, and apply relentless pressure to enemy forces. Its short Weapon Range requires smart positioning, but in the right hands, this mech is a nightmare for any opponent caught within its fiery reach! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/a0dd648cd84c24ba9d45d60d0a6c31d07dff6aac.gif[/img]

[h2]ABILITY PAIRINGS[/h2] 
Consider these combinations for maximum effectiveness: 
[list]
[*] [b]Archie Miller – Mech Jet:[/b] With moderate Health, the Draqan relies on mobility to stay alive. The Mech Jet allows it to leap across the battlefield, helping it close the gap on enemies or reposition quickly when overwhelmed. The landing impact deals damage, making it an excellent opener before unleashing its high-speed flamethrower attacks. 
[*] [b]Jan Novak – Deploy Mines:[/b] Since the Draqan excels in close-quarters combat but lacks defensive durability, Deploy Mines reinforces your zone control. Enemies forced to move through chokepoints will take heavy mine damage before reaching the Draqan, making it easier to capitalize on its high Weakness Damage bonus and incinerate opponents as they stagger through its fiery range. 
[*] [b]Emilia Rochefort – Mechano-arm:[/b] With moderate Health and no built-in Repair or Armor, the Draqan can’t afford prolonged fights without support. The Mechano-arm provides health regeneration, ensuring it can remain on the frontlines longer. This is especially useful as the Draqan can continue melting enemies without retreating too often. 
[/list]

These ability pairings help the Draqan become an unstoppable force in battle, turning its short-range but relentless firepower into a game-changing advantage.

We trust this intel will aid your assessment of the Draqan! When deployed effectively, this firestorm of a mech can dominate the battlefield, forcing enemies to retreat or be reduced to ashes. Stay tuned for further reports on the remaining mechs.

notes.title: Mech Analysis: The Ironclad
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders! 

Today’s briefing contains an analysis of the Ironclad, brought to you be Sebika Ballistics. This mech is a perfect example of a Jack of All Trades. You’re in good hands when one of these reliable and well-balanced machines is on the squad.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/d61a0f539572889724d237268df189ba0e6042ab.jpg[/img]
[h2]KEY STATISTICS [/h2]

The Ironclad has respectable stats across the board. Belonging to the Ballistic Class, it’s mode of attack relies on two mounted machine guns with a high Fire Rate and consistent Damage. Take advantage of this by choosing on-hit effects and increased Critical Chance when applying Module Upgrades or Enhancements from the battlefield! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/83049c4f2cdbb9f4e583daef37c82503794de88f.gif[/img]

With decent Health, Move Speed, and Weapon Range, this mech is well-suited for manoeuvring across the map to wherever it’s needed. This means it can consistently collect Enhancement drops, complete objectives, or defend against enemy waves.

[h2]ABILITY PAIRINGS [/h2]

As an all-rounder, the Ironclad can make effective use of all three of your original Pilots’ Abilities: 

[list]
[*] [b]Archie Miller - Mech Jet:[/b] the additional manoeuvrability provided by the Mech Jet allows the Ironclad to effectively deal with most situations and act as the “runner” for the squad. It will also save the day by jumping in to crush any unfortunate enemies on areas it chooses to land. 
[*] [b]Jan Novak - Deploy Mines:[/b] the Ironclad is well-suited to zone control, especially when defending a particular point. Deploy Mines will help you lock-down areas of the map. 
[*] [b]Emelia Rochefort - Mechano-arm:[/b] as a mid-range unit in terms of Health, the Ironclad benefits hugely from the additional sustain of the Mechano-arm. Use this ability to help it take point when in combat and relieve pressure from the rest of your squad. 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/818d0c6b55559c25c01745f1719c461158ffd1f2.gif[/img]

We trust this intel will inform your consideration of the Ironclad! When put to good use, it can stablise your team who can rest easy knowing it has their back. Stay tuned for further reports on the remaining mech models.

notes.title: Resistance Pilot Profile: Emilia Rochefort
notes.content:
It’s time you got to know the pilots under your command in Grit and Valor - 1949. 

In the coming weeks, we’ll be sharing some detailed intel on our brave Resistance pilots and how you can make the most of their abilities on the battlefield. Starting with Emilia Rochefort!

[h2]Emilia Rochefort: Repair Pilot[/h2]
[b]Nationality: [/b]French
[b]Age:[/b] 22
[b]Special Ability:[/b] Mech Repair

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/0c438b193f812b797c3fe1ff8f8ef059577f674f.png[/img]

[b]Biography[/b]
Growing up on a farm in a rural Alsace village, Emilia was fascinated with the way things worked. From an early age she’d take apart her toys and household appliances just to put them back together again. She was always tinkering with something. As she grew older, she began repairing and greatly enhancing her family farm’s agricultural equipment. 

By 18 she'd already become an immensely talented engineer, but when the Axis invaded Emilia's family farm was reduced to ash. She joined the Resistance soon after, applying her exceptional skills to the Resistance’s new Mech Command division.  
  
[b]Personality Traits[/b]
Emilia is deeply curious, always seeking to understand the "why" behind everything. Her unmatched resilience drives her to believe that nothing—whether a machine or a mech—is beyond repair. This hopeful outlook drives her on the battlefield where she is pragmatic, focused, and unwavering. 
  
[h2]Pilot Special Ability: Mech Repair[/h2] 
Naturally, Emilia Rochefort’s mechanical prowess allows her to make on-the-fly repairs to the mechs she pilots on the battlefield.  
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/25e6a368a4dcdf9bcf8307c8267aa9e74a376a81.gif[/img]
 
This Ability can be effective in several ways. Use it offensively – deploying Emilia’s mech on the front line and effectively turning your mech into a ‘tank’ unit, soaking up damage before repairing yourself. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/e219c57ec41b05cca188ffd4cb10fa3a7361abcb.gif[/img]

Alternatively, you can use it defensively, keeping your repair ability in reserve for a noble last stand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/10eff1192c1892d211624eca9e38caba5a1094fd.gif[/img]

Whichever way you choose to deploy it, Emilia's Special Ability can have a significant impact on your chances of surviving a run - so be sure to use it!

notes.title: Grit and Valor – 1949 | End of Year Roundup
notes.content:
[b]Commanders, it’s been a glorious year for the Resistance.[/b]  

To cap off our 2024, we’re rounding up some of our Grit and Valor highlights and briefly hinting at what’s to come in 2025. 

[h2]Unveiling Grit and Valor – 1949[/h2]

May 30th 2024, was the day we revealed Grit and Valor to the world. To cast your mind back, here’s a look at that very first reveal trailer.  
 
[previewyoutube=QReoFOX8Y2k;full][/previewyoutube]
 
In our [url=https://www.milkytea.com/grit-announce]press release[/url] we described the game as “A dieselpunk real-time tactics roguelite...set in an alternate reality Europe where World War 2 rages on and the Evil Axis controls the continent. As the last hope to end this brutal conflict, players must join the resistance and escort an EMP device into the heart of enemy territory and destroy their mech production and communications headquarters – Machine Tower.”  
 
We were massively grateful for the positive reaction this initial announcement received – it spurred us on to get something playable into your hands... 

[h2]Our First Public Demo[/h2]

July was a big one for us. Just over a month after our announcement, we released our first public demo. We were eager to bring you along with us for the journey, and allow you to provide direct feedback to help shape the future of our game. 
 
[previewyoutube=ZxVolxS9pGg;full][/previewyoutube] 
 
It was also significant for us to see swathes of great influencers and content creators getting to grips with their mech squads. Our teams were thrilled to see people they were already big fans of - such as [url=https://www.twitch.tv/barbarousking]Barbarous King[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GAVBHNoPahs&t=164s]Splattercatgaming[/url] - experiencing something they’d had a hand in creating!  
 
[h2]Taking Grit on the Road[/h2]

We’ve also been lucky enough to bring Grit to players, press, and industry heads at a bunch of events throughout the year.
 
In June, shortly after its announcement, Grit and Valor had a presence on the show floor at Guerilla Collective’s ‘The Mix’ event in LA.  
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/b42f635d864ec1b1f9188e652e8c240d20b2632a.jpg[/img]
 
Later, in August, the Grit Team were in Seattle during PAX West to showcase Grit once more at a great Guerilla Collective event.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/2bcceea026e57bfe7afe01381389b32fcdee0dbd.jpg[/img]
 
Then in late September, Grit had something of a homecoming when we brought it to FORMAT Liverpool – held a stone’s throw from the studio in which it’s being developed.  
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/44ae0a26ca6f33ea79dea40ad9f0dd267127123f.jpg[/img]

We’re eagerly anticipating further events appearances in 2025.  
 
[h2]The British Isles Boss Reveal[/h2]

Boss Battles were absent from our first demo, and remained a well-kept secret here at Grit and Valor HQ. 
 
In November, however, we let the cat out of the bag with our British Isles Boss Reveal. 
 
[previewyoutube=5G1qwG7b9tE;full][/previewyoutube]
 
[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=estRGnnmBEE]PirateSoftware’s stream[/url] then detailed this entirely new aspect of gameplay. We’re really proud of the way it changes the dynamic of Grit’s strategic play.  

[h2]Our Closed Beta[/h2]

Instead of winding-down for the festive period, we ramped up. In early December we launched a closed beta, giving players access to both the British Isles and Scandinavian campaigns as well as their respective boss levels.  
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/5cbd841b3e1c717d97493e027f96b0b1e35a42e4.png[/img]
 
Mid-way through the ‘closed’ beta – we decided to open it up to everyone, allowing you to get hands-on with an improved version of the game that you’ve helped us shape.  
 
This made it our largest playtest yet, and we’re grateful to have a treasure trove of fresh feedback to delve into in the new year. 

[h3]A Special Thanks For Your Support![/h3]

To our honourable Commanders,

Ahead of 2025, we’d like to take a moment to sincerely thank you all for your contributions to Grit and Valor.  
 
Your support - be it providing insightful feedback, sharing our content, or simply interacting with us across socials or in our Discord– has been fundamental in helping us build a head of steam on the track to launch. 
 
What’s next, you ask? Well, in case you missed our last update, a second public demo is coming at some point in Q1.  
 
And then? Launch!  
 
Happy Holidays to you, Commanders.   
We’ll see you when you report back for duty in 2025. 
 
The Grit and Valor Team

notes.title: Upcoming Features Deep Dive #1 – Run Rewards!
notes.content:
[b]Attention, Commanders! [/b]
 
We've received fresh intel on upcoming changes to Grit and Valor’s Run Rewards systems. 
 
As mentioned previously, your feedback on the demo has been helping our teams massively in finding new ways to make Grit’s tactical gameplay sing.  

Now that the Closed Beta is live, we’re going to be delving in to a wealth of additional feedback. Here’s an overview of some changes to rewards that are already in the works! 

[h2]WHAT ARE RUN REWARDS?[/h2]

If you’re a Roguelite/Roguelike veteran – feel free to skip ahead! 
 
If you’re new to Roguelites, a ‘Run’ is what you begin each time you’re defeated on the battlefield. 
 
Run Rewards, then, represent the progression you make over the course of a run. 
 
To make matters more complex – in Roguelites this progression can be split in two; Standard Progression and Meta Progression. 

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/13f90d87f47e56edce23befc3c61488ba353f22f.png[/img]
 
In the case of Grit and Valor – 1949, ‘Standard Progression’ represents the temporary enhancements you get during a run. 
 
‘Meta Progression’ represents the permanent upgrades you’re able to make back at the Resistance Base and carry with you in future runs. 
 
[h2]RUN REWARD IMPROVEMENTS: STANDARD PROGRESSION[/h2]

[h3]Reward Frequency[/h3]

We noticed that only offering mid-run upgrades at the end of a mission meant long breaks between upgrading your squad over the course of a run!  
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/0f61ba1d9562b87a692a5f00e42185380e7cf7d1.gif[/img]
 
In future you’ll notice rewards "dropping" during a mission. You’ll need to assess on the fly whether to bring your Mechs out of cover to go procure them, adding an entirely new risk-vs-reward dynamic to your moment-to-moment gameplay. 

[h3]Improved Enhancements[/h3] 

To make choosing enhancements and going for a specific build more meaningful, we’re going to improve their effects and even create synergies between different Enhancement types. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/d3b7279019d802ef217af8937def03005ba7a972.gif[/img]

[h2]RUN REWARD IMPROVEMENTS: META PROGRESSION[/h2]
 

[h3]New Pilots![/h3]

We’ll also be introducing some new Pilots – each with unique never-before-seen abilities! We can’t wait to tell you more about them in a later blog...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/9957fad903ee627454811c1466d9c19c867c9f8c.png[/img]
 

[h3]Pilot Ability Augmentations[/h3] 

We’re also exploring new ways to give you more control over how you set up your squad. In the future, Grit and Valor will allow you to augment existing Pilot Abilities to make them behave exactly the way you like. 
 
Take the Mech Jet Ability, for instance. With Pilot Ability Augmentations, a cautious player could augment this ability mid-run to be able to jump then immediately jump back to its starting position. Alternatively, an offensively minded Commander could augment that same ability to drop mines as it jumps. 
 
We took your feedback and some inspiration from other satisfying Roguelite systems for this! It should give you even more variety on each run! 
 
--- 

We hope this has given you some valuable insight into how we’re using your feedback to improve the game’s rewards system ahead of launch. In the coming weeks, we’ll be sharing more of these deep dives on other aspects of Grit and Valor Gameplay! 

If you’d like to help with future changes, [url=https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/LLHGHCV]apply to our Ambassador program[/url] where we hold regular playtests. You can also [url=https://discord.gg/8eqDpa88nf]join our Discord[/url] for extra behind-the-scenes content! 
 
[i]The Grit and Valor – 1949 Team[/i]
